name: Neurological Muscular Channelopathy Due to a Genetic Ryanodine Receptor Defect

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in the RYR1 gene
Presence of episodic muscle weakness or paralysis triggered by stressors such as exercise, heat, or anesthesia
Electromyographic evidence of abnormal muscle membrane excitability consistent with channelopathy
Muscle biopsy showing cores or other structural abnormalities typical of RYR1-related myopathies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pathogenic RYR1 mutation plus at least one major clinical criterion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by electrophysiological and histopathological findings but requires genetic confirmation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Episodic Muscle Weakness Triggered by Heat or Exercise
searchTerms: muscle weakness triggered by heat or exercise
episodic weakness after activity or heat
heat or exercise induced muscle weakness

pathognomonic.notes: Triggered by certain anesthetics or stress
searchTerms: risk of severe reaction to anesthesia
mild fixed weakness in upper leg muscles
difficulty breathing due to weak muscles

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase during episodes
Normal to mildly elevated baseline CK
imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective fatty infiltration and atrophy in proximal muscles
genetic: Pathogenic variants in the RYR1 gene detected by molecular genetic testing
other: Abnormal electromyography with myopathic and channelopathy features
Muscle biopsy showing cores or multi-minicores

distinguishingFeatures: CACNA1S or SCN4A gene mutations instead of RYR1
May lack episodic muscle weakness outside crises
Congenital myopathy with fixed muscle weakness
Characteristic central cores on muscle biopsy

redFlags: Rapid onset of generalized muscle weakness with respiratory compromise
Signs of malignant hyperthermia during anesthesia
Recurrent episodes of muscle paralysis triggered by heat or exercise
references: Jungbluth H, et al. Ryanodine receptor 1-related myopathies. Semin Pediatr Neurol. 2018.
Robinson R, et al. Malignant hyperthermia and RYR1 mutations: clinical and genetic aspects. Anesthesiology. 2020.
Orphanet: Neurological muscular channelopathy due to a genetic ryanodine receptor defect. ORPHA:98742.
